status: REGISTERED 2026-10-11 before any model result on revision posts (development check of the prompts on the 7 development items is the only model use before registration-time freeze; see 'rule')
question: When a public maintenance thread revises the announced window (cancelled, moved, extended), does a language-model compiler read the revision where the development rule does not, and does reading it keep more obligations in the closed loop than ignoring it?

data.items: data/maintenance_revisions_merged_20261011.json: timing-changing update posts from the 2026-09-29 and 2026-10-01 collections (scripts/analyse_notice_updates.py), usable = announcement with a clock time, update with a clock time or a cancellation, posted before the end; test 155 (Imperva 88, Linode 27, Sinch 21, UpCloud 19), development 7
data.selection_caveat: items were selected by timing keywords; the action label is derived from them, so a keyword rule reproduces it (arm rule_kw is that upper bound); automatic status transitions fired for most cancelled events, so cancelled truth is the text
data.split: the part field of the merged file: computed per collection by analyse_notice_updates.py from the provider-group hash of the announcement benchmark; development 7 (New Relic 4, Supabase, Snowflake, Packet), test 155

step1_compile.targets: action (descriptive) and the new bound: new start vs automatic In-progress time for moved, new end vs automatic Completed time for extended; ±2 min strict, ±60 min loose
arms: rule (development rule on the update text; no cancellation detection)
rule_kw (rule plus the selection keywords; upper bound)
step1_compile.prompts: scripts/revision_compile_eval.py DIRECT / EXTRACT, frozen at registration; announcements compiled with the announcement benchmark prompts (--target ann)
step1_compile.analysis: paired wins/losses and mean difference on the strict and loose bound, cluster bootstrap over notices (only four test providers), 10,000 resamples, seed 0; descriptive action accuracy by kind
step1_compile.runner: PYTHONPATH=src python scripts/revision_compile_eval.py models --part test --model qwen7b --model qwen72b --mode extract --mode direct --target upd|ann --out runs/revision_scenario_20261011/compile/{upd|ann}

step2_closed_loop.worlds: scripts/run_maintenance_revision.py worlds(): test items the rule can anchor (136: extended 101, cancelled 24, moved 11), path 3, 2 Mbps, 30-min clock, ns-3 seed by hash
step2_closed_loop.metric: as v2 (satisfaction over 12 intervals, hard-SLA intervals, window satisfaction where a true window exists)
step2_closed_loop.analysis: paired differences M_update_c − M_initial_c (value of reading the revision) and M_update_qwen7b_extract − M_update_rule, cluster bootstrap over notices; breakdown by truth kind; descriptive, no advance/stop verdict

rule: prompts, converter, selection and world construction are not edited after registration except by a recorded amendment before the affected step; a change after a test result forces a rerun of that step

amendments.before: step 2 model arms (rule-based arms and R0/oracle already run on all 136 worlds; no model closed-loop result yet)
amendments.text: Closed-loop analysis restricted to the cancelled and moved worlds (35). The 101 extended worlds are uninformative by construction: the maintenance is already in progress from interval 0 at 2 Mbps, every arm including the oracle scores 0.175 satisfaction with about 9.6 hard-SLA intervals per episode, because the end of a window is observable and the controller reacts to it; the revision only tells the controller something it will see anyway. The extended worlds stay in the run and are reported descriptively. Step 1 (compile) is unchanged and keeps all 155 items.

amendments.after: step 1 model outputs and step 2 were seen (post hoc, disclosed)
amendments.text: Action labels corrected. The selection keyword rule took the first keyword in the order cancel, reschedule, postpone, extend; 15 Sinch updates that reschedule or postpone a window and only mention cancellation in boilerplate ("if the maintenance is extended or cancelled") were labelled cancelled, and the automatic In-progress transition had fired for all of them. Strict rule (scripts/analyse_notice_updates.py kind_of): boilerplate removed, cancellation needs a cancelling phrase, moving/postponing before extending, a restated window counts as a move. Selection unchanged (same 162 items, same ids and order); labels: cancelled 24 -> 9, moved 11 -> 26 (test). Stored model outputs are re-scored (0 calls); the 15 relabelled worlds are rebuilt and rerun for every arm. Both scorings are reported. Pinned sources updated to the new analyse_notice_updates.py and item file; the earlier item file is kept as runs/revision_scenario_20261011/items_before_amendment2.json.
